flagged.sentence: 士兵的马骡则是李问起后，格兰特先答以按条文不行，李重读条款表示明白，格兰特随后主动口头准许的，没有写进条文。
1865年4月8日（原文只写“8日”，月份与年份据原文所录次日电报的日期1865年4月9日推定），联邦一方的格兰特随己方的波托马克军跟在李的后面追击；
但本文所据的段落没有写宣誓遣散和马骡宽许的实际执行经过。
but the passages this piece draws on do not describe how the paroling or the horse-and-mule allowance was actually carried out.
马骡宽许不在已写成的条文中，是格兰特当面答应李将指示留守军官办理的，本文所据段落未交代其落实情况；
原文记有宣誓遣散的执行人员安排，但本文所据段落未写执行经过；
the source records who was assigned to carry out the paroling, but the passages used here do not say how it was carried out;

S-GRANT67.title: Ulysses S. Grant, Personal Memoirs (1885–86), ch. LXVII, Wikisource
S-GRANT67.ref: en:Personal Memoirs of U. S. Grant/Chapter LXVII

episode.outcome: 李在4月9日接受书面条款，格兰特电告斯坦顿受降完成。次日两人在战线之间交谈，李拒绝在征询总统之前劝告全部南军投降，格兰特不再强求。两军军官在麦克莱恩家相聚约一小时后，格兰特率参谋离开，前往 Burkesville Junction。
episode.quote: I knew there was no use to urge him to do anything against his ideas of what was right.

additions.start: When the white flag was put out by Lee
additions.end: until I could be communicated with.
additions.why: 交代米德、谢里登犹豫的直接起因：李打出白旗，派人向两人请求停火，此时格兰特在途中联系不上。context.0 只写“李再次来信”后两人犹豫，没有说停火请求来自李，因果不清。

additions.start: I received your note of this morning on the picket-line
additions.end: I now request an interview in accordance with the offer contained in your letter of yesterday for that purpose.
additions.why: 李的第二封信明确为“交出这支军队”请求会面，这是从拒绝会面到受降会面的转折，现有证据包未收。

additions.start: I felt like anything rather than rejoicing
additions.end: the sincerity of the great mass of those who were opposed to us.
additions.why: 格兰特自己说明了心情低落的原因：不愿为一个久战而英勇的对手的失败而欢欣，同时认为对方的事业是最坏的之一。这会影响读者对 story.1 和叫停鸣炮的理解，现稿只写了心情低落。

additions.start: I determined to return to Washington at once
additions.why: 受降之后的直接后果：格兰特决定立即回华盛顿，停止采购和其他无用开支。这也解释了他次日离开阿波马托克斯的原因。

claims.sentence: 士兵的马骡则是李问起后，格兰特先答以按条文不行，李重读条款表示明白，格兰特随后主动口头准许的，没有写进条文。
claims.scope: 第67章全章，包括所录条款全文、马匹问答段，以及李的接受信

quote.quote: I told him that as the terms were written they would not; that only the officers were permitted to take their private property. He then, after reading over the terms a second time, remarked that that was clear.

claims.fix: 可保留。另注：格兰特后文说过 "acceded to the provision about the soldiers retaining their horses"，用的是 provision 一词，但所录条文中确实没有这一项。

claims.sentence: 1865年4月8日（原文只写“8日”，月份与年份据原文所录次日电报的日期1865年4月9日推定），联邦一方的格兰特随己方的波托马克军跟在李的后面追击；
claims.scope: 第67章全章：正文只写 "On the 8th"，章内没有写明 "April 8" 的地方

quote.quote: HEADQUARTERS ARMIES OF THE U. S., April 9, 1865.

claims.fix: 推定依据宜改为更直接的一件：格兰特当夜（次日）的回信就署1865年4月9日。可改作“月份与年份据格兰特次日回信所署的1865年4月9日推定”，不必绕到下午的电报。

claims.sentence: 但本文所据的段落没有写宣誓遣散和马骡宽许的实际执行经过。
claims.scope: 第67章全章已通读：只有执行人员安排，没有执行经过。格兰特次日即离开

quote.quote: Generals Gibbon, Griffin and Merritt were designated by me to carry into effect the paroling of Lee′s troops before they should start for their homes

claims.fix: 范围可写得更准确：改为“格兰特回忆录第67章全章没有写执行经过”，不要只说“所据段落”。

claims.sentence: but the passages this piece draws on do not describe how the paroling or the horse-and-mule allowance was actually carried out.

quote.quote: After an hour pleasantly passed in this way I set out on horseback, accompanied by my staff and a small escort, for Burkesville Junction

claims.fix: Say "Chapter LXVII of the memoirs does not describe…" rather than "the passages this piece draws on".

quote.quote: I would, therefore, instruct the officers I left behind to receive the paroles of his troops to let every man of the Confederate army who claimed to own a horse or mule take the animal to his home

claims.fix: 把“本文所据段落”改为“第67章全章”。

quote.quote: General Lee leaving Generals Longstreet, Gordon and Pendleton for them to confer with in order to facilitate this work

claims.sentence: the source records who was assigned to carry out the paroling, but the passages used here do not say how it was carried out;

quote.quote: Generals Gibbon, Griffin and Merritt were designated by me to carry into effect the paroling of Lee′s troops

claims.fix: Change to "Chapter LXVII does not say how it was carried out"; consider merging with the horse-and-mule sentence.

claims.sentence: The horses and mules belonging to the Confederate enlisted men were not in the written terms at all
claims.scope: 所录条款全文及马匹问答段

quote.quote: I told him that as the terms were written they would not

claims.sentence: 米德、谢里登、李的说法也都经他一手记录。
claims.scope: 第67章正文；章内另有出版方据帕克提供的原件所加的脚注[2]

quote.quote: The fac-simile of the terms of Lee′s surrender inserted at this place, was copied from the original document furnished the publishers through the courtesy of General Ely S. Parker

claims.fix: 对话部分属实。建议补充一点：李的两封信和接受函是以文件原文录入的，不是格兰特的转述；章内脚注[2]出自出版方，所据是帕克提供的原件。这样写比“经他一手”更准确。

context_issues.problem: 稿件只写“李再次来信”后米德、谢里登犹豫是否停火，漏掉了起因：李打出白旗，并分别派人向两人请求停火。现写法让读者以为犹豫是针对那封信。李第二封信的内容（为交出军队请求会面）也没有交代。

quote.quote: Lee, therefore, sent a flag to the rear to advise Meade and one to the front to Sheridan, saying that he had sent a message to me for the purpose of having a meeting to consult about the surrender of his army, and asked for a suspension of hostilities until I could be communicated with.

context_issues.problem: 只写格兰特心情低落，没有写他给出的理由。原文的理由与后文叫停鸣炮直接呼应；不写出来，读者容易自行补写心理，这也与 limits.1 的原则相悖。

quote.quote: I felt like anything rather than rejoicing at the downfall of a foe who had fought so long and valiantly, and had suffered so much for a cause, though that cause was, I believe, one of the worst for which a people ever fought

context_issues.problem: 段落停在李拒绝劝降，读者看不到格兰特的反应。原文紧接着写格兰特不再强求，随后两军军官互访叙旧。

quote.quote: I knew there was no use to urge him to do anything against his ideas of what was right.

context_issues.problem: “全文只有一个史源，即格兰特本人的回忆记述”不够准确：章内脚注[2]出自出版方，依据是帕克提供的条款原件；书中还以原文收录了李的信件。“一个史源”是指一本书，不应读成书中一切内容都是格兰特的转述。

quote.quote: There is a popular error to the effect that Generals Grant and Lee each signed the articles of surrender.

review.overall: S-GRANT67 已通读全文。各条否定性断言在全章范围内成立，但应把核查范围从“本文所据段落”改为“第67章全章”。context.0 漏掉了李请求停火这一起因，必须修改；另有几处次要的上下文补充。
